issues.description: Raising PerformanceWarning as a hard exception is a category error; warnings are not exceptions.
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass meant for warnings.warn(), but the code raises it to abort the write. The name lies about the behavior, and the test enshrines it with pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning). Either rename to a proper Error subclass and raise, or call warnings.warn and let the caller proceed. Pick one contract.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` is dead code signaling an undecided fail-fast vs warn-and-continue contract.
issues.detail: The `break` immediately following `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` can never execute. It indicates the author was unsure whether to report all misaligned axes or stop on the first. Decide the policy explicitly (fail-fast or aggregate) and delete the dead statement.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` uses `max(1, dtype.itemsize)` which papers over a case that should be explicit.
issues.detail: numpy itemsize is always >= 1 for real dtypes, so the guard is either dead code or hiding an unhandled case (object/structured dtypes). The expression also exposes an internal computation to the user as a recommended config value. Drop the defensive max or handle the edge case explicitly; write `z.dtype.itemsize * int(np.prod(zarr_write_chunks))`.

issues.description: Inline 20-line validation tangled with rechunk dispatch should be extracted to a small pure helper.
issues.detail: Computing dask_write_chunks, iterating axes, formatting the error, and the region branch all live inline in to_zarr. Extract a pure `validate_shard_alignment(zarr_chunks, dask_chunks, dtype) -> Optional[str]` (or `_resolve_write_chunks`) so to_zarr decides the action. This separates write-mechanism from config-resolution policy.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is brittle and reads backwards; use `% zw != 0`.
issues.detail: Operator precedence happens to make this work, but a reader must re-derive it. Write `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` for obvious intent. Clarity over cleverness on a guard clause.

issues.description: PR ships a `raise` while the description openly asks whether raising is correct; policy is undecided.
issues.detail: The author asks whether exception-or-warning is right when config competes with shard shape, but the diff already raises. Docstring says "performance warning," message says "avoid risk of data loss," code raises. Three stories. Decide the contract before merge and align code, tests, docstring, and message.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying idea — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned chunks — is sound, but the validation block is not ready to land. The dominant defects are a category error (raising a `PerformanceWarning` class as a fatal exception, cemented by the test) and literal dead code (`break` after `raise`) that reveals an undecided fail-fast vs warn-and-continue contract. Secondary issues include suspicious `max(1, itemsize)` math, a brittle `not x % y == 0` expression, and an inline 20-line guard that wants to be a pure helper. The PR description itself asks a policy question the code has already silently answered — decide warn-vs-raise, name the class accordingly, extract the helper, and resubmit.
